Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call yesterday — quick follow-up from our procurement side. We have two related asks before we can route a PO through our S2P system: 1) Can Redwood accept a conditional PO (single PO referencing multiple service clusters) where discounts only vest after cumulative usage thresholds are met across entities? Our legal/finance wants explicit language in the PO memo so the ERP matches rebate triggers. 2) We operate a weekly invoice run for some of our business units and a monthly run for corporate. Can you confirm invoice cadence is supported per-PO (weekly vs. monthly) and whether early invoices (ad-hoc proforma) are possible for launch credits?

Attachments: clearpath-po-example.xlsx (example PO format)

If you can point me to the exact field names Redwood needs in the PO memo (e.g., "discount_band=Silver;threshold=500k"), that'd help our AP team map it.

Appreciate it — Jordan

Subject: Re: PO mechanics question re: pricing pack eligibility and invoicing cadence

Jordan — thanks, this is clear and helpful. Short answers up front: yes to conditional POs with cumulative threshold gating, and yes to per-PO invoice cadence (we can honor weekly or monthly runs depending on the PO header). A couple of clarifying notes and a recommended minimal PO memo format below.

Key points:
- Discount vesting: We can support discounts that vest once cumulative spend across specified entities reaches a threshold. The PO must list the entity IDs and a single PO number that maps to the commercial commitment (we will rely on your PO memo to trigger our billing rules).
- Memo fields we recommend (exact text recommended in quotes so your ERP can copy/paste):
  • "redwood_pricing_pack": <pack_name>
  • "discount_band": <Bronze|Silver|Gold>
  • "cumulative_threshold_usd": <integer value>
  • "entities_in_scope": <comma-separated entity IDs>
  • "invoice_cadence": <weekly|monthly|ad-hoc>
  • "early_invoice_allowed": <true|false>

- Early/proforma invoices: possible but require pre-approval and a separate "proforma" flag in the memo (we use this to route to our finance ops team).
- Holdbacks: if Clearpath requires a contractual holdback until thresholds are met, we can accept it but will need an explicit holdback schedule in the memo and a contact for reconciliation.

I attached a one-page pricing-pack breakdown and a small PO worksheet template that maps the fields we need. See attached: pricing-pack-breakdown-2026Q4.pdf and Redwood_PO_worksheet_template.xlsx.

Next step: If that works, can you share a sample PO with the suggested memo fields filled? Ben (cc'd) will review the template for any contractual language, and Vanessa will confirm accounting-side mechanics for weekly invoice routing.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Naomi — perfect, thanks for the template. I've filled the fields on a draft PO and attached it to this thread (draft PO name: CP-PO-Redwood-Draft-20261106.docx). A couple of quick clarifications from our side:
- We will include entities_in_scope as "CP-EAST,CP-WEST,CP-CORP" and set cumulative_threshold_usd to 500000. Is that threshold evaluated on invoice recognition or cash-received? Our accounting prefers invoice recognition.
- For early invoices: we'll mark early_invoice_allowed=true for a one-time proforma to cover launch credits, but the AP team wants the proforma to be labeled clearly so it doesn't hit payment runs.

If invoice recognition is acceptable for the threshold, we should be able to proceed. Expect the draft PO in your inbox within the hour.
